# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm first to act in this round... wait, actually the order is Mute, Blind, Deaf - so I act last. Let me check if there's anything from Mute or Blind first. This is turn 1, viewable context is empty, so no one has spoken yet this round to me.

I should share what I see, since Blind needs this information relayed (through Mute, or I could speak directly to Blind too, but Blind can't hear... wait, Blind CAN hear, just can't see or touch-read visuals). Let me recheck: Blind cannot see a color, gesture, or anything printed - but can they hear? Yes, "Blind: Reach the bomb" with no "cannot hear" listed. So Blind can hear my speech.

I should speak the bomb's details so Blind (and Mute) receive it. Mute needs this to cross-reference with the manual.

```
speak(text="Display shows 0. Light is yellow. There is one large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: 1 is red, 2 is blue, 3 is green.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute gestured "✌" to me - that's 2 fingers. Since Mute can't speak to me via gesture with words, this is likely a signal. Since I can see gestures from Mute, this could mean "wire 2" or "condition 2" or something referencing a manual entry. But I don't have context on what it means yet. Let me wait for more info or ask Blind/Mute for clarification - but I can't hear Mute's speech anyway, and Mute can't speak at all (Mute cannot speak, only gesture to me since I can see).

Since Mute cannot speak, all Mute's communication to me is via gesture only. Mute might be trying to indicate something about wire 2, or a step number, or count of something in the manual matching what I described.

I should acknowledge and maybe try to get more info by offering more detail, since Mute might need to confirm specific attributes match manual conditions.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows 0, light yellow, button large labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Mute signaled something about wire 2 or a count of 2 - waiting for more clarity.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute is repeating the same gesture "✌" (2). This suggests it's a stable signal, likely pointing to wire 2 or confirming something with 2 in it. Since Mute reads the manual and I see the bomb, Mute might be trying to ask me a yes/no question or indicate a specific wire to check, but without more gesture vocabulary established, this is ambiguous.

Let me try establishing a simple gesture protocol back to Mute - since I can gesture too, and Mute can see gestures. I should try responding with a gesture referencing wire 2's color (blue) somehow, but Mute doesn't know my color-to-symbol mapping yet.

Actually, since I can speak (Mute receives my words) and I can also gesture (Mute receives gestures), and Mute cannot speak but can gesture back to me - we have a full bidirectional channel via gesture+speech combo! I speak/gesture to Mute, Mute gestures to me.

Let me ask Mute a direct question via speech that they can answer with gestures (like thumbs up/down).

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see wire 2 is blue. Is wire 2 the one to cut? Gesture thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed with 👍 (thumbs up) that wire 2 (blue) is the one to cut. This came after my question, so it landed in this round after Mute's turn... wait, turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf each round. Mute already acted this round before I could ask. So this 👍 is actually responding to my question from last round now. Good, confirmed: cut wire 2 (blue).

Now I need to relay this to Blind, since Blind is the one who can act but cannot see my gestures or read anything printed - Blind can only hear speech. I should speak to Blind directly to tell them to cut wire 2 (blue).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 2, the blue wire. Mute confirmed this is correct.")
wait()
```
